subject: Edgemap: Post-call tech recap + latency/throughput playbook
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgemap.com>, Sam Cho <sam.cho@edgemap.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Edgemap: Post-call tech recap + latency/throughput playbook

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff:

Pain points you called out:
- Current hosted stack is hitting p95 latency spikes ~250-350ms under load (esp. peak concurrent sessions).
- Throughput drops during 2-3pm PST peak; request burstiness causes queueing.
- Security: inference must run in a customer VPC and meet their audit log retention policy.

Business goals (what success looks like):
- Interactive chat: target p95 <= 200ms end-to-end for median requests (avg ~350 tokens).
- Sustained concurrent throughput: 150–200 RPS with 95th percentile latency goal.
- Controlled unit cost; explore quantized model variants to reduce GPU footprint.

Technical notes we captured on the call:
- Typical request payload: ~350 tokens in, expect ~160 tokens generation.
- Peak seq length: up to 512 tokens for some workflows.
- Security: must be deployed into EdgeMap VPC (no external model proxies).

Attached: edgemap-initial-metrics.csv — your exported telemetry sample.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Alex/Sam: confirm any additional non-functional requirements (retention, encryption, auditors) by EOD Friday.
2) Redwood (Vivek + Ben): produce a lightweight SLO playbook and an initial topology recommendation for your concurrency profile by Tuesday 8/11.
3) Agree POC window (we suggest 2 weeks with a 48-hour load test in week 2).

If these look good I’ll loop Ben in to draft the benchmark steps.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Edgemap: Post-call tech recap + latency/throughput playbook

Thanks Neha — this is a good summary. A couple clarifications and the additional telemetry you asked for are below.

Clarifications from our side:
- Current p95 numbers: the bulk of the spikes are around 280–320ms; tail events up to ~520ms when bursts queue.
- Target concurrency: sustained 150 RPS; burst to 220 RPS for short windows (1–5 minutes).
- Average prompt size: ~350 tokens in; average generation ~160 tokens out.
- We have strict VPC-only deployment requirement and HSM-backed KMS for keys.

I attached a short breakdown (inline) from our infra team with heap and GPU utilization during the spike window. We can open a direct SFTP for larger exports if helpful.

Also: we want to evaluate both streaming and non-streaming modes — streaming for chat UX, non-streaming for batch reranks.

If Redwood can give a topology that keeps 95th <= 200ms for streams at 150 RPS (and a plan for handling bursts to 220 RPS), we’ll be ready to move to a paid POC.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
VP Product, EdgeMap Inc.
alex.rivera@edgemap.com

Subject: Internal: Edgemap POC — topology & SLO draft (for bench prep)

Vivek / Ben —

Forwarding the EdgeMap clarifications (see Alex’s reply). Key asks: p95 <= 200ms at 150 RPS sustained, burst to 220. Must be VPC-only and support streaming.

High-level plan I want us to validate in the bench:
- Models to test: redwood-rt-large-quant (8-bit), redwood-rt-xl-16b, and the equivalent float32 variant for baseline.
- Deployment modes: Dedicated reserved pool (primary) + regional fallback (secondary) to hit burst/availability targets.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up on queue depth, with warm-up pool of 2 instances to reduce cold-start tail.
- KV/prefix caching: enable for common prompts to shave tokens at the start.

Proposed SLOs to present to the customer (draft):
- p50 latency (streaming start): <= 80ms
- p95 latency (end-to-end): <= 200ms
- Sustained throughput: 150 RPS at p95 target
- Burst handling: tolerate 220 RPS for up to 5 minutes with degraded p95 <= 350ms and graceful queuing

Please draft a bench script that exercises: streaming latency, non-streaming batch throughput, and burst patterns. Attach the initial proposal pdf and I’ll send to Alex for visibility after you both sign off.

Timeline: bench plan + SLO doc by 8/11 EOD; run bench 8/12–8/13; share results 8/14.

Thanks —
Neha

Subject: Redwood proposed topology & timeline — Edgemap POC (draft)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Attaching a short SLO proposal and a recommended topology for the POC. Summary below:

Recommended POC topology (week 1):
- Dedicated pool: 3 x p4d-equivalent instances (optimized for streaming) running quantized model profile (redwood-rt-large-quant).
- Warm standby: 1 instance kept warm to reduce cold-start tail during bursts.
- Autoscaling: policy triggers scale-up at queue depth > 25 or CPU/GPU util > 70% sustained for 60s.
- Regional fallback: route overflow to a secondary region (within the same cloud provider) with model parity; traffic-shift policy to bleed 10% at a time.

POC acceptance criteria (draft):
- p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 200ms at 150 RPS for 30-minute sustained window.
- Maintain correctness: no more than 1% regression vs. your current model outputs on the reference prompt-set.
- Audit/logging: sample-level request+response logs pushed to your S3 bucket in the VPC for 30-day retention.

Next steps to finalize:
1) Alex: confirm that the proposed warm-standby count (1) and the p4d-equivalent instance class match your expectations. If not, tell us the exact instance family you prefer.
2) EdgeMap sign-off on the SLOs and the POC dates (we’re aiming to start 2026-08-12).
3) Execute an NDA/POC order form — I can send a DocuSign link once you confirm scope.

Docs attached: redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf
